scope_note: Production remained fully live and untouched (read-only connections only) throughout. All writes targeted ONLY database/_p5a_migration_build/replacement_main.db and a new database/_p5a_migration_build/cold_segments/transfer_index_cold_2026_08_delta.sqlite segment file. hot_boundary_source: docs/audits/storage_lifecycle_p5a_part14_row_accounting.json (hot_boundary_unix, 90-day rolling window frozen at P5A's freeze time) -- literal recorded value reused, not re-derived
identity_key: (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, block_time) composite, per P5A Part 15 corrected methodology -- raw id NOT used since cold segments locally renumber ids

candidate_pre_existing_state_finding.observation: database/_p5a_migration_build/replacement_main.db already contained 80,693 rows with id > P5A_HIGH_WATER (6648855) BEFORE this session's script ran, and a cold delta segment did not yet exist.
candidate_pre_existing_state_finding.root_cause_investigation: Verified all 80,693 pre-existing rows byte-identical (full composite-key match against production for the same ids, 80,693/80,693 matched, 0 mismatches). Checked the superseded storage_lifecycle_p5b_pre_cutover.json (the FIRST P5B attempt, HOLD_P5B_UNEXPECTED_WRITER verdict) -- that artifact explicitly states 'action_taken: NONE beyond read-only reconnaissance. No delta copied,' so it is NOT the source. database/_p5a_migration_build/ is gitignored (no commits reference it), so its exact prior-session origin cannot be traced via git history. Origin is therefore UNRESOLVED but the rows themselves are independently VERIFIED CORRECT (byte-identical to production, correctly HOT-classifiable), so this poses no integrity risk to Stage 1's own output.
candidate_pre_existing_state_finding.disposition: Not a defect and not blocking. INSERT OR IGNORE correctly treated these as already-present and inserted only the 1 genuinely-new row this session found. Documented here transparently rather than silently absorbed; flagged for human awareness that the candidate build directory has untracked prior write activity of unknown session origin, though verified benign.

hot_write_result.note: 80,692 of the 80,693 hot-classified rows were already present in replacement_main.db from a prior partial sync (see candidate_pre_existing_state_finding above); verified byte-identical, not overwritten (INSERT OR IGNORE).

round2.reason: MAX(id) re-checked immediately after round 1 completed; production high-water was still 6743251 (unchanged). No new rows arrived during round 1's ~82s execution window, so round 2 was correctly skipped per the task's 'up to 2 rounds' instruction.

final_replacement_main_db_row_count.expected: P5A original hot_total_rows (3,487,386) + total delta hot rows ever synced into this candidate across both this session and the prior partial attempt (80,693) = 3,568,079
final_replacement_main_db_row_count.no_double_insertion: Confirmed via INSERT OR IGNORE semantics + the byte-identical verification above; this session's own net new contribution was exactly 1 row.

cold_delta_segment_verification.collision_check: No pre-existing 2026_08 segment found among the 41 original P5A segments (all 41 cover months through 2026_05 per P5A's own record); distinct '_delta' suffix used regardless per instruction to avoid any future naming ambiguity with a possible future full-month 2026_08 segment.
cold_delta_segment_verification.existing_41_segments_untouched: Confirmed -- this session only created and wrote to the new *_delta.sqlite file; no existing cold segment file was opened in write mode.

delta_identity_reconciliation.method: Streaming chunked XOR-combined SHA256 digest over composite key (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, block_time), identical method to P5A Part 15, restricted to the delta id range (6648855, 6743251].

disk_check.note: Delta write volume (1 HOT row + one small ~5241-row cold segment, well under 10MB) caused no measurable change to free disk; never approached the 20 GiB hard-stop or 25 GiB caution threshold at any point.

production_mutation_confirmation: Every read against database/flex_complete_database.db in Parts B and C used a read-only URI connection (file:...?mode=ro) with PRAGMA query_only=1. No write statement was ever issued against the production file. wt_ops_v2.db and local_operation_discovery_corpus.db were also opened read-only only, for pin-set loading.
